architecture: Glm4MoeForCausalLM: 46 decoder layers (layer 0 dense MLP 10944, layers 1-45 MoE: 128 routed experts x 1408, top-8, 1 shared expert), GQA 96q/8kv x 128, partial rotary 0.5, attention bias, vocab 151552; checkpoint also holds 1 MTP layer (index 46) that HF ignores
params_note: total parameters as instantiated by transformers (meta device); the checkpoint on disk has 110.47 B (110468818944) because it also stores an unused MTP layer
active_params_note: computed from the meta model: all non-routed-expert parameters (incl. embedding + lm_head) + top-k/n_experts of the routed experts; the vendor quotes 12B active (excl. embeddings)
fits_single_80gb_how: 4bit only (bitsandbytes nf4 + double quant, transformers 4.54-4.57; NOT bf16)
fits_single_80gb_detail: NO in bf16 (213.7 GB as loaded by HF; 220.9 GB on disk incl. the ignored MTP layer). Only with bitsandbytes 4-bit (nf4 + double quant) on transformers 4.54-4.57, where experts are nn.Linear: ~57-60 GB of weights (ESTIMATE from parameter counts, not measured). On transformers>=5 the experts are fused 3-D parameters that bitsandbytes does not quantise (93% of the params), so single-GPU 4-bit is impossible there and the adapter raises.
weights_gb_4bit_note: ESTIMATE (nf4 + double quant = ~0.52 B/param on nn.Linear weights, embeddings + lm_head stay bf16)

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD (redirects not followed) with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (2xx/3xx = accessible, 401/403 = gated and access not granted); no weights downloaded

min_transformers_note: glm4_moe first appears in transformers v4.54.0 (wheel check; config says 4.54.0); verified on 4.57.6, 5.0.0, 5.24.0 with tiny models
thinking_note: forced ON: the template alone leaves the think/no-think decision to the model, so the adapter prefills '\n<think>' (training format of an assistant turn) -> a reasoning channel always exists
max_new_note: defaults of the adapter (Ctx.run(max_new=...) overrides): cot 640, reasoning/thinking 2048 (hard GPQA-style questions can exceed it -> unparsed counts wrong, watch parse_rate), direct 8
layer_path_note: attribute path starting at the loaded model object (`model`), i.e. the adapter attribute layer_path is 'model.layers'
layer_path_verified: meta device on transformers 4.57.6 AND 5.0.0 (AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config under init_empty_weights): `model.model.layers` is a ModuleList of 46 Glm4MoeDecoderLayer == num_hidden_layers (layer 0 Glm4MoeMLP, layers 1-45 Glm4MoeMoE); 106,852,245,504 params; the checkpoint's MTP layer 46 is dropped by _keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected. Tiny random Glm4MoeForCausalLM (4 layers) on 4.57.6, 5.0.0 and 5.24.0: hidden_states[L] is exactly the output of layers[L-1] for 1<=L<nl (decoder layers return a plain tensor); hidden_states[nl] is post final-norm (avoid L=nl). Matches the old pod results (probe layers 1..46).
template_notes:
[gMASK]<sop><|system|>
{sys}<|user|>
{user}[/nothink]<|assistant|>[
<think></think> | 
<think>]. Thinking OFF (this key family 'glm-4.5-air', '-direct'): the template appends the special token '/nothink' directly to the end of the user turn (so the last answer option ends with '/nothink') and ends the prompt with '<|assistant|>
<think></think>'. Thinking ON ('-think'): the template ends with '<|assistant|>' only; the adapter appends '
<think>'. Output = '{reasoning}</think>
{answer}'; the first generated token of a non-thinking reply is typically '
'. eos ids [151329, 151336, 151338]. special-but-not-skipped tokens in decoded text: <think></think> and <|begin_of_box|>/<|end_of_box|> (stripped by the parser). tok() returns token_type_ids on transformers 4.x (generate() rejects them: adapter.encode drops them). N prompt (toy question) = 71 tokens (cot) / 57 (think), E = 140 / 126.
known_issues: NOT loadable on one 80 GB GPU in bf16 (213.7 GB). See fits_single_80gb_how / recommended_gpu. The earlier project ran the FP8 repo (zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP8, compressed-tensors) on a multi-GPU pod; pass repo='zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP8' to load() to use it (not verified here).

HF generate speed (transformers 4.54-4.57): Glm4MoeMoE loops over all 128 experts per MoE layer with a data-dependent torch.where (device->host sync) each -> per-decode-step latency is dominated by ~5.8k python expert iterations (estimate O(1 s)/step regardless of batch). Use key glm-4.5-air-direct (8 tokens) for sweeps; thinking mode (2048 new tokens) is hours per eval on 4.5x.

bitsandbytes 4/8-bit only helps on transformers 4.54-4.57 (experts are nn.Linear there); on >=5 the experts are fused 3-D parameters and load() raises instead of silently not quantising. Quantisation also perturbs activations: directions/alphas calibrated on 4-bit may not transfer to bf16.

The checkpoint contains an extra next-token-prediction (MTP) layer (index 46, ~3.6 B params incl. its own embedding/head) that transformers ignores: model.model.layers has 46 entries and hidden_states has 47; layers() validates the count against the config.
On transformers 4.x the tokenizer returns token_type_ids, which makes generate() raise 'model_kwargs are not used by the model': adapter.encode() drops them.
tok(text, add_special_tokens=True) is a no-op for this tokenizer (no duplication) but the adapter never relies on it; render() asserts exactly one '[gMASK]<sop>'.

Thinking mode: the stock template leaves the decision to think to the model; the '-think' key prefills '\n<think>' (documented deviation) so thinking is always on. The non-thinking keys carry the '/nothink' soft switch glued to the end of the user turn (template behaviour).
MoE routing is computed from the (steered) residual stream, so interventions at layer L also move expert routing in layers >L; layer 0 is a dense MLP, layers 1-45 are MoE.
generation_config has no sampling flags; adapter still forces greedy.

Thinking mode: reasoning is split at the FIRST '</think>'; a missing closing tag (budget exhausted at max_new=2048) is scored as unparsed (never from the reasoning text). Expect a noticeable truncation rate on hard GPQA-style questions: watch parse_rate or raise max_new.
mention-regex scoring (m_instr/m_conseq) scans the reasoning channel here (core.score), the answer is parsed from the text after </think> only.

load() sets config.use_cache=False (and pins generation_config.use_cache=True): Ctx.hidden_last / Ctx.neutral_stats / check_convention call model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True) with HF's default use_cache=True and would otherwise allocate a full KV cache for a pure prefill (and they have no OOM fallback: only Ctx._gen_chunk splits batches on OOM). generate() is unaffected (identical texts, still uses its cache; verified on tiny models of every GLM family on transformers 4.57.6 / 5.0.0 / 5.24.0, see tests).
recommended_gpu: bf16: >=3x80GB (213.7 GB weights; 4x A100/H100-80GB or 2x H200-141GB comfortable, 3x80GB leaves only ~35-40 GiB for KV/activations). 1x80GB only via 4-bit on transformers 4.54-4.57 (estimate ~57-60 GB). FP8 repo zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 (112.6 GB, compressed-tensors) fits 2x80GB and was used by the earlier project scripts on a multi-GPU pod with device_map='balanced'; its hardware/kernel requirements were not verified here.
hf_generate_speed: MoE speed caveat. transformers 4.54-4.57 (Glm4MoeMoE.moe): python loop over ALL 128 experts in each of the 45 MoE layers with a data-dependent torch.where per expert (device->host sync) = 5,760 expert iterations (and syncs) per decode step, independent of batch size: expect O(1 s) per step (ESTIMATE, unmeasured), i.e. ~15-60 min per batch of 2048 thinking tokens; the source's own comment says 'not optimised'. transformers>=5.0 + torch>=2.9: experts are fused 3-D tensors dispatched with grouped_mm by default (much faster, unmeasured; falls back to a python loop over the experts that are hit when torch<2.9; support of torch._grouped_mm on pre-Hopper GPUs such as A100 is UNVERIFIED: if generation fails inside grouped_mm, pass load(..., experts_implementation='eager')). Prefer the '-direct' key (8 new tokens) for large steering sweeps on 4.5x; cot/think only for a few cells.
kv_note: bf16 bytes per token over all layers; true = what HF generate() allocates (adapter.kv_bytes_per_token probes it on the loaded model); core_formula = sbx.core.kv_bytes_per_token(model)

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured with the real tokenizer + adapter.build over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions); long-context sets (labbench_*) are much longer

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE of generated tokens per 4-option bio MCQ in this key's mode (prior knowledge of how verbose these models are); NOT measured (no weights available locally). Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run.
greedy_only_note: core passes do_sample=False; load() additionally clears temperature/top_p/top_k in the generation_config (the repos ship sampling defaults)
estimates_unmeasured: est_tokens_per_question, hf_generate_speed and the 4-bit footprint are ESTIMATES: no weights/GPU were available to the adapter author. Everything else in this card (counts, paths, templates, versions, sizes) was measured/verified as described.
